storyboard.title: Who gets a fix, and when
storyboard.subtitle: From php.net to a running server: the ladder a fix climbs down, and the versions it never reaches. 9 panels.
storyboard.rule: Every line a character says is the storyboard's own words, not a quote, and is marked not_a_quote; every evidence panel quotes this site's data word for word and names the file (quote_from), which the gate checks; every panel cites the evidence vault's source slugs it rests on (cites), which the gate checks against the manifest.

scenes.title: Who gets a fix, and when
scenes.subtitle: From a tag on php-src to a restarted worker
scenes.note: Who this is for: Drew, who rebuilds, redeploys and restarts.

scenes.caption: How a fix reaches a server
scenes.note: Tags at 13:35 UTC and the advisory at 14:00 on 21 October; the first OS package in the NCSC-NL inventory (Red Hat) at 15:30; Ubuntu, Debian and the Docker image by 16:03.

scenes.caption: The supported branches

cast.says: Four branches, four releases, signed tags.

scenes.note: The full engine change, in the CVE records.

scenes.caption: The branches past their end of life
scenes.note: End-of-life branches got at most a minimal source backport; none is in the CVE records.

scenes.caption: Downstream products, at 15:28 UTC on 22 October
scenes.note: Read commit by commit from the public NCSC-NL list; one row has no status.

scenes.caption: Installed is not running
scenes.note: The fix is live only when every PHP process has been restarted on the new binary.

evidence.quote: If that cannot happen today, apply the temporary settings, put a firewall in front, and as a last resort take the system offline.
evidence.source: this site, What should be done? (data/plain.json)

scenes.caption: Check the box you deployed to

cast.says: How do I know my host did it?
Ask for the version running, not the one installed.

scenes.note: The question for a host: which PHP version is serving my site right now, and when was it restarted.

scenes.punchline: A fix counts when the worker restarts on it.
scenes.note: Every rung, every downstream row and its status, on /patching/.

cast.what: The cast of PHP October 2026's storyboards, v0.1, proposed by storyboard@php.newsroom on 22 October 2026 for the editor to accept, change or replace. Drawn programmatically by the storyboard kit v0.1.0 (vendored from api.storyboards.sgit.ai, hashes in assets/vendor/storyboards/VENDOR.md) from 'look'; nothing here is an image. Fictional people, each named after one of this site's readers (data/personas.json), so a storyboard can be read as that reader's briefing; one agent, the Desk, who speaks only for the evidence; and Mallory, the name cryptography has long given an attacker. No real person is drawn. Every human uses they/them, because the readers they are named after have no stated pronouns.

characters.name: The Desk
characters.role: the newsroom's voice: says only what the evidence vault and this site's data say, with the status word attached
characters.stands_for: the team of agents behind this site, speaking with one voice
characters.personality: calm, exact, never rounds a number up
characters.wants: every reader to leave knowing which facts are confirmed and which are only reported
characters.fears: a headline number repeated without what it measures
characters.line: Confirmed, reported, or not known yet. Pick one.

characters.name: Casey
characters.role: the website owner: runs a shop on WordPress with a hosting company
characters.stands_for: the reader on /briefings/site-owner/: plain English, wants to know what to ask the host
characters.personality: practical, a little anxious, writes things down
characters.wants: to know whether to do anything today
characters.fears: waking up to a hacked site
characters.line: Just tell me what to ask my host.

characters.name: Sam
characters.role: the security lead: decides what is patched first and when a system goes offline
characters.personality: dry, sceptical, reads the advisory before the headline
characters.fears: a quiet compromise found in a month
characters.line: Attempts are not compromises. Show me a compromise.

characters.name: Drew
characters.role: the PHP and platform engineer: rebuilds, redeploys and restarts
characters.personality: quick, terse, lives in a terminal
characters.wants: the version numbers and the commands
characters.fears: a fix that is installed but never restarted
characters.line: Installed is not running. Restart it.

characters.name: Rowan
characters.role: the journalist: has to write the number in the headline
characters.personality: curious, fast, asks who said it first

characters.name: Jordan
characters.role: the board member: owns the risk, not the servers
characters.personality: patient, asks one question at a time
characters.wants: to know who decides to pull a system offline
characters.fears: learning about it from the news

characters.name: Mallory
characters.role: the attacker: scans the internet for servers that have not installed the fix
characters.stands_for: every party sending php2shell requests; who they are is not known
characters.fears: a patched, restarted server behind an edge rule
